name: Hyssop
overview: Scripture reveals hyssop as a significant plant indigenous to Western Asia and Northern Africa, used by the Israelites in various sacred rites. It played a crucial role in the Passover, where a bunch of hyssop was dipped in the blood of the paschal lamb and applied to doorposts for protection (Exodus 12:22). Hyssop was also integral in purification ceremonies and sacrifices of separation, as described in Leviticus 14, where it was combined with cedar wood, scarlet, and birds to cleanse both people and houses. Additionally, hyssop is connected figuratively to spiritual cleansing, pointing to its deeper symbolic meaning beyond physical rituals.
